description.narrative: The Uganda programme “Improving Quality and Inclusive Education for Girls and Boys in Karamoja: A life Course Approach” (2023-2027) is led by UNICEF, working in collaboration with the Ministry of Education and Sports (MoES), 9 District Local Governments of Karamoja; the teachers’ college in Moroto, schools, community leaders and a number of civil society partners in Karamoja. The overall aim of the programme is to ensure that girls and boys in Karamoja, aged 3–19 years, progressively achieve age-appropriate learning outcomes by 2027. UNICEF and partners aim to attain this through a comprehensive approach that encompasses pre-primary, primary and secondary school age children, adolescents, their parents, and target communities – the life course approach, in an integrated manner. The programme is being delivered through system strengthening; capacity building; and community engagement. Three specific outputs are expected: Output 1: By 2027, boys and girls aged 3–5 years, particularly the rural and urban poor in Karamoja, access quality and inclusive Early Childhood Care and Education through school and community-based learning spaces. Output 2: By 2027, girls and boys demonstrate increased learning achievement in literacy and numeracy through increased access to inclusive, equitable and relevant quality education. Output 3: By 2027, adolescent girls and boys demonstrate increased learning achievement through increased access to safe, gender-responsive equitable learning environments. The programme seeks to address the complex socio-cultural issues that inhibit access to and completion of quality and equitable education. The interventions focus on equitable access; quality of classroom interaction; capacity and motivation of teachers; education supervision and school governance; data management, M&E systems; supporting safe and gender-transformative learning environments. Other activities include supporting the MoES to develop, review, disseminate relevant policy documents, such as a draft inclusion policy that addressing disability, special needs as well targeting through support to early detection of disabilities and to children with disabilities and developmental delays
